The tie is quotable line by line in the study's own processing script - all 35 gad_* codes are produced by dplyr::rename() from the raw form header that contains the item wording (Question_framing_data_processing.Rmd lines 234-276 for Study 1 and 821-861 for Study 2), and the 5 dimension stems and 7 symptom rows parsed out of those 35 headers partition exactly 5x7=35 with no leftovers, matching the 35 live item codes one to one. No statistical route was run and none is needed; what this does NOT establish is anything about the two arms' differing presentation, which is disclosed in the public_note instead.

Live data, 62 complete cases of 71. Correlation of each item with the sum of the sixteen items claimed to be negatively worded: CES4 -0.16, CES8 -0.08, CES12 -0.39, CES16 -0.14 (all negative) against +0.23 to +0.61 for the other sixteen (min CES13 0.226, max CES18/CES20 0.61) -- a clean gap with no overlap. The four claimed reverse items intercorrelate +0.26 to +0.55 among themselves, and their means are 2.31-2.66 against 0.10-0.89 for the rest. The source paper states 'Four items (4, 8, 12, 16) are reverse-scored', so the polarity signature falls on exactly the four codes canonical CES-D numbering predicts. Supporting route 8: among the sixteen negatively worded items the highest mean is CES11 'My sleep was restless' (0.89) and the lowest CES9 'I thought my life had been a failure' (0.10), the expected ordering in a nursing-home elderly sample. This does NOT distinguish CES4 from CES8/CES12/CES16, and does NOT order the sixteen negatively worded items among themselves -- no per-item statistics are published for this sample and all 20 items share one 0-3 scale, so no route separates them. PARTIAL, not VERIFIED.

Cronbach's alpha of UCLA1-8 as stored in the live table = 0.7111 vs the paper's published .71 (diff 0.0011); the deposit's own Loneliness composite equals mean(UCLA1..8) with max abs difference 0.0 across all 71 respondents, matching the ULS-8 'average the 8 item scores' rule -- together these establish that these eight codes are the ULS-8 and that the stored values are the SCORED (already reverse-coded) values. Item-rest correlations are all positive (UCLA1 0.614, UCLA2 0.377, UCLA3 0.120, UCLA4 0.565, UCLA5 0.687, UCLA6 0.247, UCLA7 0.211, UCLA8 0.400), so no positively-worded item is stored raw. The reverse-worded pair is identified as {UCLA3, UCLA6}: they are each other's strongest correlate (r=0.295) and re-flipping them costs the least alpha of all 28 pairs (0.6071; next best {3,7} 0.5989, worst {1,5} -0.6425), matching the paper's 'Two of the eight items were reverse-coded' and the canonical ULS-8 reverse pair. This does NOT distinguish the six negatively-worded stems from one another across UCLA1/2/4/5/7/8, nor separate UCLA3 from UCLA6; those rest on the canonical ULS-8 numbering alone. Hence PARTIAL.
